The problem is that the GPU market in general isn't really competitive at all right now.

AMD just prices its GPUs according to the formula "Nvidia minus some small offset", with no desire to increase market share or consumer good will, while Nvidia further ramps up prices with every generation.

The high prices also mean very high profit margins for both, Nvidia and AMD. They won't do anything that provokes a price war, since financially, the current situation is what's "best for business and shareholder interests" - maximum revenue with the least amount of effort and units produced/sold.

Consumers used to be the no. 1 priority, but not anymore. So essentially, the market is controlled by a duopoly came to an unspoken agreement based on a shared motive of greed.

Intel is willing to undercut them, but neither the HW, nor the drivers are quite there yet. Its architecture heavily relies on per-title driver optimizations, which isn't ideal. Battlemage suggests a positive trend though - hopefully it continues with Celestial.

These days, I always recommend buying a higher-tier GPU from a previous generation on the used market, instead of a new entry level one, except for when someone absolutely demands a certain feature or characteristic (i.e. lower pwr-draw, FSR4, wanting to hit a certain performance target with RT, etc.).

text:
These RX9060XT cards are about 5-10% faster than my RX6700XT, which was my upgrade from a RX580 two years ago. My RX580 was only a 4GB card, but it played everything fine up to about 2020 with settings set mostly to high (some very high) with only shadows turned way down as that always tanked the FPS.

I've found that in most of games I own the visual difference between high or V.High vs Ultra/Epic... was so small you would have to do screen captures to tell them apart. The big difference is that on Ultra/Epic type setting the games use maximum resolution textures for objects that are at a distance rather than using smaller images, often for objects on screen that are so small it is irrelavent.

Also playing super-epic-ultra mode does not make a boring game any better to play, proof being that replaying Half-Life 2 or Portal today is still as much fun as it was 20+ years ago, or playing Borderlands or Dishonoured that have cartoon'ish visuals anyway. HL2 and Portal can be played with everything set to maximum using the iGPU of my Ryzen 7900 (that just 2 RDNA 3 CUs. I know because I tried it before moving the 6700XT over and my new PC and it ran at 90 to 120 FPS.
